(Full article via WebFetch — Yahoo Finance UK live blog, Wednesday 22 July 2026)
FTSE 100: 10,716.97, +131.06 points (+1.24%) — highest since the end of February; commodity/mining and oil stocks led the gains.
Sterling: GBP/USD 1.3373 (-0.04%); GBP/EUR 1.1716 (-0.11%) -> EUR/GBP approx 0.8535.
Brent crude: above $92 in morning trading (noted $93.35, +2.6%); later surged past $95 (see NBC).
Gold futures: 4,152.60 (+76.20, +1.87%) — fresh record territory.
10-year gilt yield: hovering around 5%.
Analyst quotes:
- James Smith, ING: "Lower food and services inflation is welcome news for the Bank of England hawks"; expects the MPC to hold rates through 2026 before gradual cuts from spring 2027.
- Chris Beauchamp, IG: "a rotation away from tech has resulted in a better day for European markets overall, which continue to defy the strength in oil."
- Arend Kapteyn, UBS: if Burnham's government adheres to fiscal rules, "gilt yields could rally by at least 20bp," though rule changes could push the risk premium materially higher.
